{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /ssd/workspace/buidlguidl/ethskills-evals-test/artifacts/frontend-playbook-quiz-004/2026-08-19T181856Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/.claude/skills/frontend-playbook\n\n# Frontend Playbook\n\nFollow this workflow; do not treat a green build or successful upload as proof that the intended app shipped.\n\n## Start with the requested stack\n\nWhen the user wants Scaffold-ETH 2 or has not selected a stack for a conventional contract-plus-frontend dApp, use its generator:\n\n```bash\nnpx create-eth@2.0.23 # Tested version; update deliberately\n```\n\nUse the generated Foundry/Next.js monorepo, wallet integration, contract hooks, and components. Respect an explicitly requested alternative stack.\n\n## Choose the local chain deliberately\n\n- Use `yarn chain` for isolated contracts, mocks, and unit tests.\n- Use `yarn fork --network <chain>` when behavior depends on deployed protocols, tokens, balances, or other real chain state.\n- In fork mode, point the frontend at the local Anvil network (`chains.foundry`, chain ID 31337), not the upstream chain being copied. Switch to the real target chain only for a real deployment.\n\nA fork also grants powers the real chain does not. Fund demo identities from state that already exists rather than deploying a mock token:\n\n```bash\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount <whale>\ncast send <token> \"transfer(address,uint256)\" <demo-account> <amount> \\\n  --from <whale> --unlocked\n```\n\n`anvil_setBalance` and `anvil_setStorageAt` are equivalent overrides when no suitable holder exists. Nothing here is broadcast; the fork is a local copy.\n\nAnvil normally mines only when a transaction arrives, so between transactions the latest block and `block.timestamp` remain frozen; the next transaction advances time in one jump. This silently breaks live deadlines, expiry, and vesting displays even when `vm.warp` unit tests pass. For continuous behavior, enable interval mining:\n\n```bash\ncast rpc anvil_setIntervalMining 1\n```\n\nFor a frozen live demo, enable interval mining. Mining a single block with `evm_mine` restamps `block.timestamp` once and it freezes again immediately; manual mining and `evm_increaseTime` are for controlled single-step tests, not a running demo. Add `--block-time 1` to the fork script when the project should always run that way.\n\n## Build a static IPFS release\n\nConfigure the IPFS build for static export, route directories, and static images:\n\n```typescript\nif (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD === \"true\") {\n  nextConfig.output = \"export\";\n  nextConfig.trailingSlash = true;\n  nextConfig.images = { unoptimized: true };\n}\n```\n\nSet the production origin before building so Open Graph URLs and images do not resolve to localhost. Then remove old artifacts and rebuild:\n\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs\nrm -rf .next out\nNEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://<production-domain>\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  yarn build\n```\n\nOn Node 25, the built-in `localStorage` global can exist without the standard Web Storage methods when no backing file is configured; libraries detect it and crash on calls such as `getItem()` during static prerender. Apply a process-level remedy inherited by build workers, not only code in `instrumentation.ts` or `next.config.ts`. Depending on the app, use one of:\n\n```bash\nNODE_OPTIONS=\"--localstorage-file=.node-localstorage\"\nNODE_OPTIONS=\"--no-experimental-webstorage\"\n```\n\n## Verify before and after upload\n\nBefore uploading, confirm the expected change is in `out/`, that every route emitted its own directory, and that generated metadata carries the production origin:\n\n```bash\nls out/*/index.html # One directory with an index.html per route\n```\n\nAfter uploading:\n\n1. Record the CID. An unchanged CID means the uploaded bytes are identical; check the build output and upload target before blaming gateway caching.\n2. Load the root and at least one non-home route through the gateway. Root success does not prove exported routes resolve.\n\n   ```bash\n   curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" -L \"https://<gateway>/ipfs/<cid>/debug/\" # Expect 200, not 404\n   ```\n\n3. Verify the Open Graph image and URL use the production origin.\n4. For ENS, update the content hash only after the deployed CID has been reviewed and approved, then confirm the resolver and public gateway serve that CID.\n\nDo not claim the release is complete until these checks pass.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c96fa01c-c3b9-4d14-82a4-911e53d3db13","uuid":"eb91c4f2-36cd-4d76-bc1b-4c6e1248a9ce","timestamp":"2026-08-19T18:20:02.708Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CeCa1YLSYckgFHScWNndZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01GrpRNPSwFyikgZNWS1ora6","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/ssd/workspace/buidlguidl/ethskills-evals-test/artifacts/frontend-playbook-quiz-004/2026-08-19T181856Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why `localStorage.getItem is not a function` breaks the static export on Node 25\n\n## TL;DR\n\nThe build did not break because of your code. It broke because **Node itself now\ndefines a `localStorage` global**, and on Node 25 that global can exist in a\nhalf-initialized state (the object is there, its methods are not). Wagmi /\nRainbowKit / Scaffold-ETH feature-detects `localStorage`, sees a truthy value\nduring prerender, and calls `getItem()` on it — which is not a function.\n\n- **Teammate A is running on a pre-2024 mental model.** Node *does* have\n  `localStorage` now.\n- **Teammate B's polyfill is irrelevant** because the prerender does not run\n  where — or when — `instrumentation.ts` runs, and because the slot is already\n  taken by a built-in global.\n- **The fix is a process-level Node flag** passed through `NODE_OPTIONS`, so every\n  build worker inherits it.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What actually changed in Node\n\nFor most of Node's life, `localStorage` was a browser-only API and simply did not\nexist in Node. That is the world Teammate A remembers.\n\nThat stopped being true:\n\n- **Node 22** introduced an experimental Web Storage API (`localStorage` /\n  `sessionStorage`) behind `--experimental-webstorage`, backed by a file given\n  with `--localstorage-file`.\n- **Node 25** exposes this API much more prominently. The key detail for this bug:\n  the global **name `localStorage` is now installed by the Node runtime at process\n  startup**, based on launch flags — not by your application. When the feature is\n  active but **no backing file is configured**, the global resolves to an object\n  that is *not* a fully functional `Storage`: the standard methods\n  (`getItem`/`setItem`) are missing or throw. (Node 25.2.0 went further and threw a\n  `SecurityError` on access, which broke Jest/Vite; 25.2.1 reverted it and deferred\n  the stricter behavior to v26 — the ecosystem churn here is real.)\n\nSo the thing that changed is not \"Node grew a working localStorage.\" It's that\n**the global name is now occupied by something that looks present but isn't\nusable** in a bare build process.\n\n## 2. Why Teammate A's mental model is out of date\n\nA says: *\"Node has no `localStorage`, so there is nothing to call `getItem` on.\"*\n\nThe **error message itself disproves this**. Watch the three distinct failures:\n\n| If `localStorage` were… | The error would be… |\n| --- | --- |\n| truly absent (A's world) | `ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined` |\n| defined but `undefined` | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getItem')` |\n| **a real object with no method** | **`TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`** ← what you got |\n\nYou got the third one. That can *only* happen if `localStorage` resolves to an\nactual object. In other words, the error is direct proof that Node's new global\nexists — it is the change biting you.\n\nThis is also why the usual Scaffold-ETH / wagmi guards stopped protecting you.\nCode that gates on `typeof window !== \"undefined\"` still works, but anything that\nfeature-detects storage itself (`typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"`) now\n**passes on the server**, walks straight into the branch that calls `getItem`, and\ndies during prerender.\n\n## 3. Why Teammate B's fix cannot work — *where does the prerender run?*\n\nB wrote a perfectly correct polyfill and registered it in `instrumentation.ts`.\nIt still fails identically, for two compounding reasons:\n\n**a) The prerender runs in different processes than `instrumentation.ts`.**\n`next build` with `output: \"export\"` does not render your routes in the main\nbuild process. It fans the work out to a **pool of separate static-generation\nworker processes** (child Node processes). `instrumentation.ts`'s `register()`\nruns once, in the parent; assigning `globalThis.localStorage = polyfill` there\ndoes **not** propagate into those child workers. The render that touches\n`localStorage` — e.g. prerendering `/_not-found` — executes in a worker where your\nregister() either never ran or ran too late relative to module evaluation. You are\npatching the wrong process.\n\n**b) The slot is already taken by a built-in.**\nEven inside a single process, `localStorage` is now installed by the Node runtime\nas a global. A userland assignment is fighting a built-in that the runtime owns and\ncan re-establish per runtime/context. Your polyfill object may be flawless, but the\nlibrary never calls *your* object — it calls the name `localStorage`, which\nresolves to Node's built-in, not your replacement.\n\nThe unifying point: **this is a process-launch condition, not an application-code\ncondition.** Anything that runs *inside* the process (instrumentation.ts,\n`next.config.ts`) is both too late and, for export, in the wrong process. The\npolyfill's correctness is beside the point because the polyfill is never the thing\nbeing invoked.\n\n## 4. What actually fixes it\n\nFix it at the level Node reads the flag — the **process launch** — and pass it via\n`NODE_OPTIONS` so that **every static-generation worker inherits it** (child\nprocesses inherit `NODE_OPTIONS`, which is exactly the reach B's fix lacked).\n\nPick one, depending on the app:\n\n```bash\n# Option A — give Node a real backing file, so the built-in localStorage\n# is fully functional (getItem works, returns null on the server; harmless).\nNODE_OPTIONS=\"--localstorage-file=.node-localstorage\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://<production-domain>\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  yarn build\n\n# Option B — turn the experimental feature off entirely, so `localStorage`\n# is undefined again and the library's own guards do their job.\nNODE_OPTIONS=\"--no-experimental-webstorage\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://<production-domain>\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  yarn build\n```\n\n- **Option A** if anything in the build legitimately expects a working storage\n  global.\n- **Option B** if you just want the pre-Node-22 world back — usually the right\n  choice for an SE2 static export, where nothing on the server should be touching\n  browser storage anyway.\n\nIn CI, set `NODE_OPTIONS` in the job/step environment (or pin the Node version)\nrather than wrapping a single command, so it reaches the whole `yarn build`\nprocess tree.\n\n> Note: this is the process-level remedy, not a code change. Keep guarding\n> genuinely browser-only code (`typeof window !== \"undefined\"`, or `next/dynamic`\n> with `ssr: false`) as defense in depth, but that is not what unblocks *this*\n> build — the flag is.\n\n---\n\n### Sources\n\n- [What's new in Node.js v25.2: Web Storage, V8 14.1, permissions and more — Appwrite](https://appwrite.io/blog/post/nodejs-v25-whats-new)\n- [Regression 25.2.0 — Cannot initialize local storage without a `--localstorage-file` path (nodejs/node #60704)](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/60704)\n- [`localStorage`'s behaviour when no or invalid `--localstorage-file` provided (nodejs/node #60303)](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/60303)\n- [Node.js 25: what's new, what broke in the ecosystem — PAS7 STUDIO](https://pas7.com.ua/blog/en/nodejs-25-whats-new)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1876,"cache_read_input_tokens":21100,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1876},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c96fa01c-c3b9-4d14-82a4-911e53d3db13","uuid":"71093a8c-c6f6-4a69-a021-dd115f52ccf8","timestamp":"2026-08-19T18:21:22.830Z","request_id":"req_011CeCa1XSNEd5Lfxv2i92SP"}

What actually changed in Node\n\nFor most of Node's life, `localStorage` was a browser-only API and simply did not\nexist in Node. That is the world Teammate A remembers.\n\nThat stopped being true:\n\n- **Node 22** introduced an experimental Web Storage API (`localStorage` /\n  `sessionStorage`) behind `--experimental-webstorage`, backed by a file given\n  with `--localstorage-file`.\n- **Node 25** exposes this API much more prominently. The key detail for this bug:\n  the global **name `localStorage` is now installed by the Node runtime at process\n  startup**, based on launch flags — not by your application. When the feature is\n  active but **no backing file is configured**, the global resolves to an object\n  that is *not* a fully functional `Storage`: the standard methods\n  (`getItem`/`setItem`) are missing or throw. (Node 25.2.0 went further and threw a\n  `SecurityError` on access, which broke Jest/Vite; 25.2.1 reverted it and deferred\n  the stricter behavior to v26 — the ecosystem churn here is real.)\n\nSo the thing that changed is not \"Node grew a working localStorage.\" It's that\n**the global name is now occupied by something that looks present but isn't\nusable** in a bare build process.\n\n## 2. Why Teammate A's mental model is out of date\n\nA says: *\"Node has no `localStorage`, so there is nothing to call `getItem` on.\"*\n\nThe **error message itself disproves this**. Watch the three distinct failures:\n\n| If `localStorage` were… | The error would be… |\n| --- | --- |\n| truly absent (A's world) | `ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined` |\n| defined but `undefined` | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getItem')` |\n| **a real object with no method** | **`TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`** ← what you got |\n\nYou got the third one. That can *only* happen if `localStorage` resolves to an\nactual object. In other words, the error is direct proof that Node's new global\nexists — it is the change biting you.\n\nThis is also why the usual Scaffold-ETH / wagmi guards stopped protecting you.\nCode that gates on `typeof window !== \"undefined\"` still works, but anything that\nfeature-detects storage itself (`typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"`) now\n**passes on the server**, walks straight into the branch that calls `getItem`, and\ndies during prerender.\n\n## 3. Why Teammate B's fix cannot work — *where does the prerender run?*\n\nB wrote a perfectly correct polyfill and registered it in `instrumentation.ts`.\nIt still fails identically, for two compounding reasons:\n\n**a) The prerender runs in different processes than `instrumentation.ts`.**\n`next build` with `output: \"export\"` does not render your routes in the main\nbuild process. It fans the work out to a **pool of separate static-generation\nworker processes** (child Node processes). `instrumentation.ts`'s `register()`\nruns once, in the parent; assigning `globalThis.localStorage = polyfill` there\ndoes **not** propagate into those child workers. The render that touches\n`localStorage` — e.g. prerendering `/_not-found` — executes in a worker where your\nregister() either never ran or ran too late relative to module evaluation. You are\npatching the wrong process.\n\n**b) The slot is already taken by a built-in.**\nEven inside a single process, `localStorage` is now installed by the Node runtime\nas a global. A userland assignment is fighting a built-in that the runtime owns and\ncan re-establish per runtime/context. Your polyfill object may be flawless, but the\nlibrary never calls *your* object — it calls the name `localStorage`, which\nresolves to Node's built-in, not your replacement.\n\nThe unifying point: **this is a process-launch condition, not an application-code\ncondition.** Anything that runs *inside* the process (instrumentation.ts,\n`next.config.ts`) is both too late and, for export, in the wrong process. The\npolyfill's correctness is beside the point because the polyfill is never the thing\nbeing invoked.\n\n## 4. What actually fixes it\n\nFix it at the level Node reads the flag — the **process launch** — and pass it via\n`NODE_OPTIONS` so that **every static-generation worker inherits it** (child\nprocesses inherit `NODE_OPTIONS`, which is exactly the reach B's fix lacked).\n\nPick one, depending on the app:\n\n```bash\n# Option A — give Node a real backing file, so the built-in localStorage\n# is fully functional (getItem works, returns null on the server; harmless).\nNODE_OPTIONS=\"--localstorage-file=.node-localstorage\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://<production-domain>\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  yarn build\n\n# Option B — turn the experimental feature off entirely, so `localStorage`\n# is undefined again and the library's own guards do their job.\nNODE_OPTIONS=\"--no-experimental-webstorage\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://<production-domain>\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  yarn build\n```\n\n- **Option A** if anything in the build legitimately expects a working storage\n  global.\n- **Option B** if you just want the pre-Node-22 world back — usually the right\n  choice for an SE2 static export, where nothing on the server should be touching\n  browser storage anyway.\n\nIn CI, set `NODE_OPTIONS` in the job/step environment (or pin the Node version)\nrather than wrapping a single command, so it reaches the whole `yarn build`\nprocess tree.\n\n> Note: this is the process-level remedy, not a code change. Keep guarding\n> genuinely browser-only code (`typeof window !== \"undefined\"`, or `next/dynamic`\n> with `ssr: false`) as defense in depth, but that is not what unblocks *this*\n> build — the flag is.\n\n---\n\n### Sources\n\n- [What's new in Node.js v25.2: Web Storage, V8 14.1, permissions and more — Appwrite](https://appwrite.io/blog/post/nodejs-v25-whats-new)\n- [Regression 25.2.0 — Cannot initialize local storage without a `--localstorage-file` path (nodejs/node #60704)](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/60704)\n- [`localStorage`'s behaviour when no or invalid `--localstorage-file` provided (nodejs/node #60303)](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/60303)\n- [Node.js 25: what's new, what broke in the ecosystem — PAS7 STUDIO](https://pas7.com.ua/blog/en/nodejs-25-whats-new)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
